Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Toxic Emissions & Waste Key
Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)
outputs are determined. Toxic Emissions & Waste is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI
ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on the potential environmental contamination and toxic or
carcinogenic emissions arising from their operations and the strength of their environmental
management systems.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Risks associated with this Key Issue
• Increased costs from liabilities associated with damaging health, property.
• Loss of access to markets through community opposition, heightened regulatory hurdles.
• Increased costs to meet compliance standards and install equipment and systems to contain
pollution.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Toxic Emissions & Waste Governance and Strategy score
The Toxic Emissions & Waste Governance and Strategy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to
govern and manage toxic emissions and waste through policies, environmental management systems,
certifications, audits, and supply chain programs. Highest initiatives reflect comprehensive policies,
certified systems, and proactive oversight across operations and suppliers. It is expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Scope and frequency of environmental impact audits
Definition: Assesses whether the company conducts regular audits to assess and manage
environmental risks and impacts. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.

o Evidence of environmental impact audits
Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence that the company conducts internal and/or
external environmental audits of its relevant operations. This could include, for example, an EMS
certified to ISO 14001 or a similar framework, which requires regular audits.
o Evidence of audits across all locations of operations
Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence of environmental audits across all locations of
operations.
o Evidence of annual environmental impact audits
Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence that the company carries out annual
environmental impact audits.
• Existence of environmental management system
Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence that the company has an Environmental Management
System (EMS) in place across all or selected relevant operations. This could include, for example, an
EMS certified to ISO 14001, registration under EMAS, or a similar framework.
• Extent of programs to reduce toxic emissions of supply chain
Definition: Indicates the extent to which the company has established programs to reduce toxic
emissions within its supply chain. Best practice is for suppliers’ environmental management to be subject
to screening and audits.
• Scope of policies to address environmental impacts
Definition: Indicates whether the company has formal policies in place to address environmental impacts
such as air emissions, water discharges, and waste.
• Certified environmental system score
Definition: Assesses the extent of the company's sites with an environmental management system
certified to ISO 14001 or similar. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating the highest degree of
certification.
o Percentage of operations with an environmental management system certified to ISO
14001 or HAZWOPER
Definition: The percentage of sites with hazardous waste guidance that follow ISO 14001 or
HAZWOPER certification for waste management.

Toxic Emissions & Waste Targets score
The Toxic Emissions & Waste Targets score evaluates the company’s initiatives to set and achieve
targets for reducing toxic emissions and waste. Highest initiatives reflect comprehensive, quantitative
reduction targets with demonstrated progress toward achievement. It is expressed as a 0–10 score,
where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Toxic emissions & waste target comprehensiveness
Definition: Assesses the extent to which a company has established toxic waste reduction targets that
have a measurable reduction scope and are complete in coverage. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10
indicating a quantitative target that covers all segments.
o Evidence of ongoing Toxic Emissions & Waste target
Definition: Indicates whether the company has an ongoing toxic emissions and/or waste
reduction target.
o Scope of ongoing Toxic Emissions & Waste target
Definition: Assess the scope of coverage of the ongoing toxic emissions and/or waste target.
Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates that the target covers all relevant segments of
the company's operations.
• Toxic emissions & waste target progress
Definition: Assesses the company’s to-date progress on active toxic emissions & waste targets, as well
as its historical track record in meeting previously stated targets. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10
indicating achievement of stated target.
o Status of ongoing Toxic Emissions & Waste target
Definition: Measures the current implementation status of the company’s ongoing target on
toxic emissions and/or waste management, by assessing the current progress against the
target.
o Status of historical Toxic Emissions & Waste target
Definition: Measures the achievement or completion status of the company’s historical
target on toxic emissions and/or waste management, by assessing whether the stated target
was achieved or not.

Toxic Emissions & Waste Performance score
The Toxic Emissions & Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on toxic
emissions and waste metrics (including NOx emissions, SOx emissions, particulate matter emissions,
hazardous and non-hazardous waste, and other relevant pollutants), relative to its peers. It is expressed
as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
• NOx emissions performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions intensity
(normalized by sales or by units of production), and trend in NOx emissions intensity, relative to its peers.
Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o NOx emissions intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions
intensity (emissions per unit of sales or production), relative to its peers. Expressed as a
0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average NOx emissions intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average NOx emissions (per
unit of sales).
 Three-year average NOx emissions intensity (production based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average NOx emissions (per
megawatt-hour generated).
o NOx emissions intensity industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of
year-over-year NOx emissions (per unit of sales or production) trend, relative to its
peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average NOx emissions intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year NOx
emissions (per unit of sales) trend.
 Three-year average NOx emissions intensity trend (production based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year NOx
emissions (per megawatt-hour generated) trend.
• SOx emissions performance relative to peers

Definition: Assesses the company's performance on sulfur oxides (SOx) emissions intensity (normalized
by sales or by units of production), and trend in SOx emissions intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed
as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o SOx emissions intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on sulfur oxide (SOx) emissions
intensity emissions (per unit of sales or production), relative to its peers. Expressed as a
0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average SOx emissions intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average SOx emissions (per unit
of sales).
 Three-year average SOx emissions intensity (production based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average SOx emissions (per
megawatt-hour generated).
o SOx emissions intensity industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-
over-year SOx emissions (per unit of sales or production) trend, relative to its peers.
Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average SOx emissions intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year SOx
emissions (per unit of sales) trend.
 Three-year average SOx emissions intensity trend (production based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year SOx
emissions (per megawatt-hour generated) trend.
• VOC emissions performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on volatile organic compounds (VOC) emissions
intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in VOC emissions intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a
0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o VOC emissions intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on volatile organic compounds (VOC)
emissions intensity (emissions per unit of sales), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

 Three-year average VOC emissions intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average VOC emissions per unit
of sales.
o VOC emissions intensity (sales based) industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-
over-year VOC emissions (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–
10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average VOC emissions intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year VOC
emissions (per unit of sales) trend.
• Particulate matter emissions performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on particulate matter (PM) emissions intensity
(normalized by sales), and trend in PM emissions intensity), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10
score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Particulate matter emissions intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on particulate matter (PM) emissions
intensity (emissions per unit of sales) relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score,
where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average particulate matter emissions intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average particulate matter
emissions (per unit of sales).
o Particulate matter emissions intensity industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-
over-year particulate matter emissions intensity (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its
industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average particulate matter emissions intensity trend (sales
based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year
particulate matter emissions intensity(per unit of sales) trend.

• Hazardous waste performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on hazardous waste intensity (normalized by sales),
and trend in hazardous waste intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10
indicates strong performance.
o Hazardous waste intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on hazardous waste generated
normalized by sales, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10
indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average hazardous waste intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average hazardous waste
generated per unit of sales.
o Hazardous waste intensity industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-
over-year hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry
peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average hazardous waste intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year
hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend.
• Non-hazardous waste performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on non-hazardous waste intensity (normalized by
sales), and trend in non-hazardous waste intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score,
where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Non-hazardous waste intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on non-hazardous waste generated
(normalized by sales), relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10
indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average non-hazardous waste intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average non-hazardous waste
generated (per unit of sales).
o Non-hazardous waste intensity industry relative trend score

Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-
over-year non-hazardous generated (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers.
Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average non-hazardous waste intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year non-
hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend.

Controversies
A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score
based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this
Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment:
• Toxic emissions and spills controversies.
For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the
Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Business Segment Exposure scores
The Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a
mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity.
MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific
adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to
calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a simple
average of the Toxicity score, Air Pollutant score, Hazardous Waste score and Radioactivity score of the
business activity:

The Toxicity score of a business activity is assessed by examining the toxicity and carcinogenicity (oral
and inhalation) risk associated with toxic emissions.
The Air Pollutant score of a business activity is assessed by taking a simple average of emissions of
carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur oxides (SOx)
and particulate matter of 10 micrometer diameter (PM10).
The Hazardous Waste score of a business activity is assessed by examining tons of hazardous waste
produced per facility.
The Radioactivity score of a business activity is assessed through a qualitative assessment of the mining
industry. Mining activities related to highly radioactive ores receive a score of 10.
Data sources
The following sources are used to determine the Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score:
The EPA’s Toxics Release Inventory, National Emissions Inventory, and Risk-Screening Environmental
Indicators; U.S. Economic Census; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; company disclosures.
